blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is a condition where your heart suddenly beats much faster than normal.
It's not usually serious, but some people may need treatment.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Causes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) happens when the electrical system that controls your heart rhythm is not working properly.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Causes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: This causes your heart to suddenly beat much faster.
It can then slow down abruptly.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Causes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: A normal resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (bpm).
But with SVT your heart rate suddenly goes above 100bpm.
This can happen when you're resting or doing exercise.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: Having supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) means your heart suddenly beats faster.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: This:

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: usually lasts for a few minutes, but can sometimes last for several hours

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: can happen several times a day or once a year – it varies

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: can be triggered by caffeine, alcohol or drugs – but often there's no obvious trigger

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: can happen at any age, but often starts for the first time in children and young adults – many people have their first symptoms between 25 and 40 years old

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: You may get no other symptoms, but sometimes people also:

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: have chest pain or discomfort

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: feel weak, breathless, lightheaded or dizzy

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Symptoms of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: feel tired

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you keep getting a fast heartbeat

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: It's important to get it checked out.
You might need a test, such as an electrocardiogram (ECG), to find out what's going on.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: you've been diagnosed with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and your episode has lasted longer than usual

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: you have a fast heartbeat with shortness of breath, chest pain or feeling faint

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: You need to go to hospital for treatment immediately.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: Do not drive yourself to A&E.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Immediate action required: Call 999 if:
s: The person you speak to at 999 will give you advice about what to do.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Things you can do to help with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: If your episodes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) only last a few minutes and do not bother you, you may not need treatment.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Things you can do to help with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: You can make changes to your lifestyle to reduce your chances of having episodes, such as:

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Things you can do to help with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: cutting down on the amount of caffeine or alcohol you drink

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Things you can do to help with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: stopping or cutting back on smoking

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Things you can do to help with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
s: Your doctor may also be able to recommend some simple techniques to help stop episodes when they happen.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Treating supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in hospital
s: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is rarely life threatening.
But you may need treatment in hospital if you keep having long episodes.

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Treating supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in hospital
s: This may include:

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Treating supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in hospital
s: medicines to control the episodes of SVT – given as tablets or through a vein

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Treating supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in hospital
s: cardioversion – a small electric shock to the heart to help it get back to a normal rhythm

blocks.path: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) > Treating supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) in hospital
s: catheter ablation – a treatment where thin tubes are placed through a vein or artery into the affected area in your heart and heat or freezing is used to correct the problem with the electrical system (this permanently cures the problem in most people)
